findings.source_quote: Γελῶ ὑμῶν τὴν μωρὰν ὑπόληψιν, ὅτι πιστεύετε ἀθάνατον εἶναι τὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ψυχήν.
findings.english_quote: I am laughing at your foolish supposition that you believe the human soul to be immortal.
findings.issue: The English makes the content of the foolish supposition the fact that the speakers believe something, introducing an unintended belief about their own believing. Simon is ridiculing their belief in the soul's immortality. Reading ὅτι causally preserves both ὑπόληψιν and πιστεύετε without this additional layer.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed replacement: “I am laughing at your foolish supposition, because you believe that the human soul is immortal.” The revised passage must undergo a fresh review.

findings.source_quote: εἰ οὖν αἱ ψυχαὶ ἀθάνατοι γίνονται καὶ κρίσις πάντως γίνεται, ὥστ’ ἂν καὶ τοὺς ἐπὶ κακῇ πράξει ὁρκισθέντας καταδικασθῆναι παρακούσαντας: πῶς οὐ πεφόβησαι σὺ ἀναγκάζειν, τῶν ἀναγκαζομένων ἐπὶ παρακοῇ κολαζομένων;
findings.english_quote: If, then, souls prove to be immortal, judgment certainly takes place, so that even those adjured to an evil deed would be condemned for disobeying. How have you not been afraid to compel them, when those being compelled are punished for disobedience?
findings.issue: The draft does not represent καὶ before κρίσις and silently treats the judgment clause as the consequence of immortality. The supplied wording and punctuation support joining immortality and judgment as a compound condition leading to the πῶς question. An apodotic interpretation of καὶ is a possible alternative, but it would require representing its “also” force and disclosing the scope decision. The existing notes do neither. This is a connective and clause-scope issue, not source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed source-transparent replacement: “If, then, souls prove to be immortal and judgment certainly takes place, so that even those adjured to an evil deed would be condemned for disobeying, how have you not been afraid to compel them, when those being compelled are punished for disobedience?” Retain the existing note on γίνονται. Alternatively, if retaining the apodotic interpretation, explicitly render καὶ as “also” and explain the competing compound-condition reading and the reason for the choice. Any revised text and notes require fresh review.
